shots.purpose: One lap that costs him. Establish his pace, let the pace be the thing that wrecks him, and land the wreck right beside Zenny so the audience sees exactly who is the bigger bee and who is the competent one. The joke is not the crash — it is the face he pulls when he realises he got away with it.
shots.performanceAssignment: He leaves at pace, chest driving ahead of his own wings, antennae proud-erect, mouth working the work song at full throttle, and goes crazy off into the distance on a wide erratic arc — shrinking to a fast dot skimming the far flower tops, never leaving frame. He comes back HARDER than he left and completely misjudges it. THE FIRST CRASH IS A REAL SMASH, NOT A BRUSH: he goes FACE-FIRST into a big flower head at full speed and the bloom ENGULFS him — he disappears into the petals entirely for a beat, the whole flower head rocking on its stem — then he bursts back out the other side completely coated in thick gold, trailing it behind him. Still travelling and half-blind with pollen he clips a second bloom, which turns him over, and the turn becomes THREE fast tight somersaults, limbs tucked, the chaos suddenly reading as accidental acrobatics — all of it at flower height, in among the blooms, never up in open sky. He comes out of the third rotation and STICKS THE LANDING on a sturdy flower head like a gymnast finishing a routine: feet planting hard, ONE LEG TUCKED BACK for balance, utterly still for a beat. Then he stands up out of it, brushes the pollen off his chest with one quick embarrassed glance round to check whether anyone saw — and, finding he is completely fine, throws a full SUPERHERO POSE: chest out, fists planted, chin up, shoulders squared, entirely too pleased with himself for a bee who just crashed twice. The line lands on that pose. Zenny's own line through this is simple and continuous: she watches him go, gives up on him, settles to her clover and works head-down through the entire wreck without once looking up at it. She is never still — she is BUSY.
shots.camera: ONE HELD POSITION FOR ALMOST THE WHOLE TAKE, THEN ONE MOTIVATED MOVE. The camera opens front-on on the pair and STAYS THERE — holding the flowers and Zenny in frame while Fuzzby goes crazy off and comes back. HE NEVER LEAVES FRAME. He goes far — shrinking to a small fast dot skimming the far flower tops deep in the field — but he stays visible the whole way out and the whole way back, and the audience never loses sight of him. The camera does not chase him; it may ease back a few inches to keep him in shot, nothing more. Zenny's eyes follow him out, then she gives up on him and settles onto the clover beneath her to work while he is still visible behind her. He comes back on the same line he went out on, faster. It does not chase him, does not go looking, and never climbs off the meadow into open sky: everything, including the tumble, plays at flower height with the blooms and Zenny in shot. It may breathe and reframe a few inches to keep the wreck and Zenny both in frame, nothing more. THE ONE REAL MOVE comes last: after his line lands, the camera DOLLIES IN on Zenny, leaving him behind in the frame, and finishes on her.
shots.openingPose: Both bees hovering at flower-top height in the open field, seen from the FRONT at the same distance from the lens — Fuzzby left of centre and clearly the larger, Zenny to his right and smaller, the size gap plainly readable because they share a depth. Low sun flaring in behind them, open sky above the flower tops, lavender spikes, white daisies and clover heads crowding the frame below them. Wings working hard on both. He is already loading to go; she is still hovering, about to settle onto the clover beneath her. Then he goes — straight off at full pace, out and away across the field, leaving her exactly where she is.
shots.cutInMotivation: This is the one junction the treatment protects on meaning alone: the dip, the sideways drag and the leaf's spring are ONE cause, and a cut anywhere inside them turns a single continuous physics chain into two unrelated events — the audience would read bad luck instead of overcommitment, and the whole reversal loses its author.
shots.dialogueBinding: Fuzzby's vocal beat performs per the approved voice design.
shots.visualPayoff: Fuzzby in a full superhero pose on the flower head — chest out, fists planted, chin up — dusty and delighted; then the camera dollies off him onto Zenny alone. She gives ONE small shrug, straight down the lens. Her face stays completely deadpan through it — flat and unimpressed, held a beat longer than is comfortable — but she is not frozen: her wings keep going and her hands keep working the clover the whole time. Only her FACE is still. Only at the very end does ONE CORNER of her mouth lift into a small wry smile. Shrug, then deadpan, then the wry corner — in that order, never together.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Fuzzby's whole body, his wings and his spectacles stay OUTSIDE the blossom and readable in silhouette through every contact — only his face and the front of his chest ever touch the pollen centre. He is never swallowed by a flower, never hidden inside it, never morphed into it.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: THE CRASH IS THE BIGGEST PHYSICAL EVENT IN THE SHOT AND IT IS BUILT IN STAGES, EACH ONE CAUSING THE NEXT: he comes in far too fast and too low; a stem clips his trailing wing and his whole body YAWS off its line; one wing corrects far too late; his face slaps square into the pollen centre of a big bloom at full speed — and it is ONE OF THE FLOWERS ALREADY STANDING IN THE OPENING FRAME, established from the first second, never a new bloom that arrives for the purpose. THE FLOWER TAKES THE FORCE, AND THAT IS WHERE THE SIZE OF THE CRASH LIVES: the head compresses flat under him, the stem bows most of the way to the ground, petals splay back, and a fat cloud of gold erupts out sideways — then the stem whips upright again and flings him off it. Neighbouring blooms are knocked nodding by the blast. He stays outside the bloom and visible for all of it. Still travelling and half-blind with gold, he clips a second head, which turns him over — the three somersaults are momentum, not choice. The landing is a hard plant onto a sturdy flower head, one leg tucked back — the head dips deep under him and rebounds, and he rides that rebound with small balance corrections. Nothing about him goes still; a stuck landing is tension held, not motion stopped. Every contact happens at flower height, in among the blooms.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A dusty bee in a full superhero pose on a flower, delighted with himself — and then the smaller bee alone in frame, who looks, sighs, stays flat, and lets one corner of her mouth go at the very last moment.
prohibitedStaging: never take the tumble up into open sky — it plays at flower height, in the blooms
never let Zenny leave frame at any point
never let the flower swallow or hide him — his body and wings stay outside it
no glow, no sparkle trail, no magic light on either bee
never write the landing as still, frozen or dead-still — it is a held pose with the flower rebounding, wings beating and balance correcting inside it
never let her smile be broad, warm, delighted or toothy — one corner only, and small
never play her shrug, her deadpan and her smile at the same time — they are three moves in order
never freeze Zenny for the deadpan — her face is flat, her wings and hands keep working
never introduce a flower for him to hit — every bloom he touches is one already visible in the opening frame
never let him leave frame on the way out — he shrinks to a dot, he does not disappear

shots.tempoDesign: SEVEN BEATS AND THE SECONDS EACH ONE OWNS. 0.0-1.0s: the pair together, wings working, frame locked on them. 1.0-3.0s: he goes crazy off at pace deep into the field, shrinking to a small fast dot but NEVER LEAVING FRAME — visible the whole way out and back; Zenny's eyes follow him out, then she gives up on him and settles to her clover. He comes back on the same line, faster. 3.0-5.5s — THE CRASH, THE BIGGEST EVENT IN THE SHOT: stem clips his wing, body yaws, wing corrects too late, face slaps the pollen centre; the head compresses flat, the stem bows to the ground, petals splay, gold erupts sideways, then the stem whips up and flings him off. 5.5-7.0s: second bloom turns him over; THREE somersaults, readable as three, at flower height. 7.0-8.5s: he STICKS the landing, one leg tucked back — a gymnast's stuck finish, tension HELD and never motion stopped: the flower dips and rebounds under him and his balance rides it. 8.5-10.5s: stands, brushes himself down with one quick embarrassed glance round to see if anyone saw, then snaps into the SUPERHERO POSE — the final spoken section lands on it. 10.5-12.0s — HER BUTTON, IN THREE SEPARATE MOVES, NEVER TOGETHER: the camera dollies off him onto Zenny alone, facing the lens. FIRST she shrugs — one small shrug, straight down the lens. THEN nothing: her face stays completely deadpan, flat and unimpressed, held a beat longer than is comfortable — but she is not frozen: her wings keep going and her hands keep working the clover the whole time. Only her FACE is still. ONLY THEN does one corner of her mouth lift into a small wry smile, and the shot lands there. Her deadpan is the joke, so it gets the most time of the three; the smile is the smallest thing in the shot.
shots.feltIntent: A four-year-old's stomach learns Fuzzby's pace, then feels it go wrong — a faceful of flower they did not see coming, then three somersaults, then a landing he has absolutely no right to. They laugh at the crash; they laugh harder at the superhero pose, because he is posing about an accident. The parent's laugh is the last frame: the small one looking down the lens like the only adult in the room.
shots.continuityProseOut: Zenny alone in frame at her blossom, facing the lens, deadpan, with one corner of her mouth just lifting into a wry smile; Fuzzby soft behind her, still in his superhero pose on the flower head, pollen still drifting.
shots.dialogueTimingProse: @Audio1 is timed to this beat, not a continuous read. It opens on 1.6 SECONDS OF SILENCE — both mouths closed. The work song runs 1.6-3.9s and is HEARD FROM ACROSS THE FIELD, quieter and duller than close because he is far away; his mouth works it out there. From 3.9s to 9.4s there is NO SPEECH AT ALL — the crash, the somersaults and the landing play in the impacts and the wing-buzz, both mouths closed throughout. At 9.4s his breath lands as he strikes the superhero pose, and 'NAILED it' follows at 9.9-10.5s, close, dry and proud. Zenny's shrug, deadpan and wry smile come after that, in the buzz, mouth closed.
shots.referenceRolesProse: Fuzzby anchor (identity: spectacles, bulbous tan nose, translucent wings, antennae) and Zenny anchor for the second bee (identity plus the size gap — Fuzzby clearly the bigger); size chart for the two-bee relationship; Buzzing Nook / wildflower scene anchor plus the scene's approved Scene Look for the field's palette, materials and light.
shots.principalPerformanceApproved: Fuzzby sings the work song at full throttle while his body performs professionalism nobody asked for — chest driving forward, antennae proud-erect, wings fast and continuous, altitude overshooting the climb then undershooting the fall. He does not aim at the blossom so much as attack it, and he commits harder than the job needs because in his head this is a display.
shots.animationTimingApproved: Fast and accelerating from the first frame: the zig-zag climb runs on quick, uneven up-down beats with no two the same length, tightening as he closes on the blossom. The dip is the one deliberate loading action — a hair longer than the beats around it. From the anthers' dump to the leaf's bow the chain runs continuous with no gaps at the joins: the sideways drag is a fast slide, the leaf's bow is heavy and slow-in as it takes his weight, and its rebound is a hard snap out. The impact runs in a stretched slow pocket of roughly a beat — everything moving, nothing held — then returns to full speed for the recovery, which builds over about a second and a half, the chest first, the head last. The drooped antenna's follow-through settles a beat AFTER the stance has finished, so the tell arrives on its own timing. Wings beat fast and continuous through every phase, including the slow pocket.

voiceDirectorBrief.speaker: Fuzzby
voiceDirectorBrief.expectedTiming: Runs across the flight and dies into the leaf; roughly 3–4 seconds of song, no dialogue over the slow pocket or the rebuilt stance.
voiceDirectorBrief.physicalActionRelationship: Voice and body telling the same lie together: the syllables land on the up-beats of the porpoise so the song sounds like it is steering him, when the flight is steering the song. The final trailing syllable coincides with the flank meeting the leaf, so the tune gets bent by the bow rather than finished.

voiceDirectorBrief.speaker: Fuzzby
voiceDirectorBrief.expectedTiming: Lands early in the shot, on the held pose, with the gold still falling past him; the eye-flick and the antenna's failed rise play out in the silence after.
voiceDirectorBrief.physicalActionRelationship: Delivered while the pose keeps building — chest pushing out one notch further on the line, glasses shedding gold, small mid-air corrections under him, wings fast beneath the dignity. The eye-flick to the drooped antenna comes AFTER the line, so the confession never contaminates the claim.

SET & LIGHT LAW (light is written in THIS vocabulary — concrete sky/sun/shadow states, never time-of-day words): Stylised feature-quality 3D CGI matching @图1. Original 3D CGI animation, ages 4-8, Pixar-caliber: real weight, squash-and-stretch, bold legible staging, character locked to reference.
REFERENCES: Use @图2 only for Zenny, @图3 only for Fuzzby and @图4 only for the round set.
FELT INTENT (the one feeling every camera, light and performance choice serves): A four-year-old's stomach learns Fuzzby's rhythm before it learns his face: stems whipping past close enough to swipe, light strobing, a body that keeps overrunning its own tempo. When the leaf throws him back out they laugh at the surprise; the parent has been reading the crowded top of frame as a promise since the first second.
OPENING ANCHOR: Begin exactly on @图1, the approved opening frame — motion begins immediately, never a resting hold.
CAMERA (storyboard-approved): The camera is his overexcited wingman: behind him, banking with him, deliberately half a beat late, horizon rolling as he rolls, and near-field leaves passing close enough to swipe the lens. It genuinely loses him at the dip behind a near-field leaf and rediscovers him already sideways and in trouble — the loss is the point, so his speed reads as something the frame cannot contain. Through the FWIP the camera must be thrown by the leaf's spring rather than choose the move: every inch of travel here has a visible physical cause in frame. Zenny must be findable, small and unremarked, in the deep background of the recovery without the camera going to look for her.
OPENING POSE / FIRST FRAME: Bee-height inside a corridor of tall rainforest flowers, the camera already travelling forward and slightly behind Fuzzby — his pollen-loaded body pitched away from us into a rising zig-zag, wings a fast blur, a rope of gold dust trailing off his hind legs, and in the near foreground a stem swinging back across the lens where he has just clipped it. Canopy shafts strobe over him as he climbs toward a ceiling of leaves that leaves him almost no headroom.
PERFORMANCE (approved physical performance): He flies the corridor as a display rather than a commute — chest driving ahead of his own wings, antennae carried proud-erect like rank, mouth working the work song at full throttle, and every zig-zag climbing higher than the flowers need before dropping lower than they need, so he is porpoising up and down inside his own zig-zag with the leaf ceiling threatening his back the whole way. He aims his head, not his line, at the blossom and drives it in past its centre; the anthers dump their loose gold onto his braced hind legs, and the new weight hanging off his back end swings his exit line sideways so he leaves the bloom flank-first and travelling wrong. His flank meets the broad leaf, the leaf's stalk takes him and bows low, and the bow's rebound throws him back up the corridor with the loose gold shearing off him. He arrests himself inside his own falling cloud and rebuilds the on-parade stance from the chest outward — shoulders back, head lifting last, wings still beating fast beneath a body that has decided to be dignified — while one antenna stays folded over and does not come up with its partner. The impact stretches into one slow pocket at the leaf — antenna whipping slow, gold hanging in the air, wings still beating fast through it — then snaps back to full speed for the recovery stance. Nothing freezes; the tempo runs slow and comes back.
INTERNAL CUTS (each becomes its own 'Shot N:' segment of the card, in this order):
  1. push closer as the zig-zag climbs into its overshoot
  2. reframe wider on the leaf's bend and spring so the throw has room to travel

From the anthers' dump to the leaf's bow the chain runs continuous with no gaps at the joins: the sideways drag is a fast slide, the leaf's bow is heavy and slow-in as it takes his weight, and its rebound is a hard snap out. The impact runs in a stretched slow pocket of roughly a beat — everything moving, nothing held — then returns to full speed for the recovery, which builds over about a second and a half, the chest first, the head last. The drooped antenna's follow-through settles a beat AFTER the stance has finished, so the tell arrives on its own timing. Wings beat fast and continuous through every phase, including the slow pocket.
GAG PHYSICS — stays visible: His wings, spectacles and the silhouette of his back through the dip
GAG PHYSICS — contact and weight: His body enters the blossom past its centre; the anthers dump loose gold onto his hind legs and the added weight pulls his exit line sideways; his flank, not his head, meets the broad leaf; the leaf's stalk compresses and bends low under his full weight, then rebounds and throws him back out along the corridor while the loose gold shears off him in a cloud. The leaf keeps oscillating after he has gone.

shots.carryMarks: the pollen coating Fuzzby's whole body from the crash, and his dishevelled fur

shots.purpose: Put the moustache on him. She comes to him, he goes back to work to impress her, and the flower gives him a face he cannot see. The audience gets the joke a full beat before he does — and her fight not to laugh is what tees up his question in the next shot.
shots.performanceAssignment: Zenny glides up beside him and simply watches him for a beat — no comment, no expression, just present, which is worse. Fuzzby takes an audience as a cue to perform: he hums LOUDER, squares up, and zooms to the next flower to show her how it is done. He does not dip into it — he drives his WHOLE FACE into the bloom, right up to the eyes, and holds there working. A beat. Then he pulls straight back out, and his entire face is caked in gold pollen in a thick band across his top lip and cheeks — a fuzzy yellow moustache he has no idea he is wearing. He is delighted with himself and completely unaware. Zenny sees it instantly. Her face fights her: the corners go, she pulls them back, her wings stutter once, and she gets it under control — but only just, and not quite. She does not laugh and she does not speak.
shots.camera: One continuous move, no cuts. It starts close on Zenny, then travels WITH her as she glides across to him, opening out into a two-shot that holds them both — her at his shoulder, him at the bloom. It stays wide enough to keep her reaction and his face in the same frame for the reveal, because the joke is both of them at once. It does not cut away for the faceplant and it does not chase him into the flower.
shots.openingPose: Begin on the handover frame: Zenny close to camera, having just let the audience in on him. She turns away from the lens and back toward Fuzzby, who stands FARTHER LEFT than her at the start of this shot — never to her right. As the camera moves with her toward him their positions may narrow, but he is never on her right at any point. She travels toward the flower head where he stands, pollen still drifting off him.
shots.cutInMotivation: Staying continuous from the FWIP would keep the audience inside his motion, and the joke needs the motion to STOP so the deadpan claim can sit in the air; the cut also changes what we know — we are now watching him rather than riding him, which is the first time the frame has an opinion about him.
shots.dialogueBinding: Fuzzby's vocal beat performs per the approved voice design.
shots.visualPayoff: Fuzzby turned to Zenny, chest out, wearing a thick gold moustache he has no idea about, having just been told exactly what he looks like; Zenny beside him having delivered the verdict absolutely flat, the effort of not laughing still visible in her face, and neither of them moving on yet.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: His striped body, his wings, his antennae and his SPECTACLES stay OUTSIDE the bloom and readable in silhouette throughout — only his face goes in, to the eyeline, and his glasses go in with it, reappearing gold-dusted on the pull-back. He is never swallowed by the flower.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: He drives face-first into the bloom and the head takes his weight, compressing and rocking on its stem while he works in it. When he pulls back the petals release him and spring; the pollen comes away ON HIM, a thick even band across the top lip and cheeks, not a dusting and not a full coating — it must read as a MOUSTACHE at a glance, shaped and sitting where a moustache sits. Loose gold puffs off the disturbed bloom behind him as he lifts clear.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A proud bee in a pollen moustache being told flatly what he looks like, and the smaller bee who told him barely moving at all.
prohibitedStaging: never let the bloom swallow him — only his face enters, his body and wings stay outside and readable

shots.tempoDesign: FIVE BEATS ACROSS TWELVE SECONDS — kept deliberately fewer than the seconds allow, so each one has room. 0.0-1.5s: we are on Zenny's face from the handover; she turns toward Fuzzby and starts to glide his way. 1.5-3.0s: she watches him, saying nothing; he takes the audience as a cue, hums louder, squares up. 3.0-5.5s — THE FACEPLANT: he drives his whole face into the bloom to the eyeline and works in there, body and wings staying outside and readable, the head rocking on its stem. 5.5-9.0s — THE REVEAL AND HIS LINE: he pulls back out wearing a thick gold moustache, delighted and unaware, and asks his question at roughly 7s, sincere, chest out. Zenny is now a body-length from him, close enough to share the frame — her face has been fighting a small continuous battle the whole time she's been in shot, corners twitching, wings stuttering, a held breath, never blank. 9.0-12.0s — HER ANSWER: she gives the verdict flat and unhurried, no grin, no build, no relish — but her face keeps its same small twitch running underneath the flatness, right through the line and into the hold. Land there: him proud and dusted, her a body-length away, still fighting it.
shots.feltIntent: The four-year-old sees the moustache the instant he does not, and that gap is the whole joke — they know something he doesn't, and they get to wait for him to find out. The parent is watching the smaller one trying not to laugh at someone she clearly loves.
shots.continuityProseIn: His gold is still falling from the leaf's throw and the leaf tip is still oscillating into the lower edge of frame; the antenna folded in the previous shot is still down.
shots.continuityProseOut: Fuzzby at the bloom wearing a thick gold pollen moustache across his top lip, proud and unaware; Zenny a body-length away with her mouth clamped and the corners twitching, wings stuttering, holding in a laugh.
shots.dialogueTimingProse: Two lines, one each, and they land LATE. The moustache must be on his face and read by the audience for a clear beat before anybody speaks — there is no dialogue at all across the hum, the faceplant or the reveal. @Audio1 is the sole source of both. Fuzzby asks at roughly 7.0s, turned to her, sincere; his mouth works only while his own words are heard and Zenny's stays closed. She answers at roughly 9.0s, flat and unhurried; her mouth works only while hers are heard and his stays closed. He does not react to the answer inside this shot — the gasp belongs to the next one.
shots.referenceRolesProse: Fuzzby anchor governs identity in close-up — spectacles, bulbous tan nose, antennae, translucent wings; the scene's Scene Look governs the bright background haze and the gold's warm morning temperature.
shots.principalPerformanceApproved: The bigger the disaster, the stiller the recovery — he holds the proud stance and delivers the reclaim absolutely dry, chest still pumped, wings fast and continuous. His eyes flick once to the drooped antenna and back out front, which is the whole confession he will ever make, and then he corrects the antenna up by hand-free will alone and it sags again.
shots.animationTimingApproved: Instant on the pose — no wind-up, he is already proud when the cut lands, which is the joke. Then the shot spends its time doing almost nothing at speed: hover corrections small and quick, wings continuous, while the gold takes the full length of the shot to fall past him. The eye-flick to the antenna is fast in, fast out, and the compensating head-lift arrives a beat after it, too late to help. The antenna's attempted rise is slow up and quick down — the collapse is the sharper of the two. The final eye-travel down the field is slow and is the last movement in the shot, arriving after the gold has cleared.

shots.purpose: Escalate the moment he has a witness — the face-plunge into the flower and the moustache it lays on him, delivered as one unbroken piece of physics so the gold is a consequence and not a trick.
shots.performanceAssignment: He arrives already committed and buries his face in the anthers, and then keeps shoving — shoulders working the head deeper as though thoroughness were measured in depth, hind legs planting and re-planting on the petal rim for purchase while both wings beat fast outside the petals and his rear end wags with the effort. The rim gives, his own shove runs out, and he hauls back the way he came, the reverse dragging his whole face across the loaded anthers as it goes. Clear of the bloom he does not check himself; he swings the chest forward, drags the shoulders back and lifts the head last into the largest on-parade stance he has struck yet, both antennae snapping proud-erect, and puts the question out front with total conviction — eyes wide open, looking at nothing on his own face, hover holding by small quick corrections while loose gold sifts off his shoulders. Nothing in him examines the result.
shots.camera: The camera stays close alongside the bloom and follows the plunge in and the reverse out on his own body's movement, then falls back a touch as he rises so the band of gold across his face is unmistakable at the moment he speaks. It must never cut away between the plunge and the reveal — the in and the out are one physical sentence — and it must never look ahead to the other bee, because his blindness to her verdict is the setup.
shots.openingPose: Bee-height alongside a wide open bloom, the camera arriving with Fuzzby as he comes in fast from behind the lens — his forward-driving silhouette crossing into frame and burying its face in the packed anthers, rear half and two beating wings left outside the petals, the bloom rocking on its stem from the hit.
shots.cutInMotivation: Remaining continuous from his boast would let the escalation read as more of the same ride; a fresh setup at the new bloom buys acceleration and a new visual idea — this is the beat where the pollen stops being cargo, and it deserves its own arrival rather than being inherited.
shots.visualPayoff: Fuzzby in a full chest-out on-parade stance just clear of the bloom, a thick band of gold laid across his face under his spectacles, antennae proud-erect, the flower he came out of still rocking behind him and loose pollen sifting off his shoulders.

shots.purpose: Abandon him mid-boast for her — the ride hits the wall. Her withholding, her ruling and the covered antenna-dip, in the flatter grammar that shuts the door on his momentum.
shots.performanceAssignment: She is working, and she keeps working: her forepaws are packing gold down into her own sacks in small even strokes, one sack shifting a fraction as it fills, while her flat stare stays aimed off-frame at him and does not move with the packing. The withholding is a task she performs — she lets his question go unanswered while she finishes a stroke, then another, sitting on the silence a fraction past comfortable, breathing shallow, eyelids low, one shoulder settling as her weight redistributes over the leaf. When she does answer, only her mouth moves and the stare does not adjust; her paws pause exactly on the last word, and one slow blink arrives after it, closing and opening late. On the final beat her antennae dip a fraction toward him, she catches it, brings them level, and drops her eyes back down to the sacks, the paws resuming the same small even strokes.
shots.camera: This frame does not move and that is the entire editorial opinion — no drift, no reassurance push-in, no consolation reframe, because the moment it breathes the two grammars stop colliding and this becomes ordinary chase coverage. Stillness is FOR the door shutting on his momentum; what stays alive inside it is her: the aim of her stare, the delay she is choosing to impose, her paws still working the sacks, and the tiny dip she catches herself making. He must stay off-screen for her ruling — his boast bought this frame and gets none of it.
shots.openingPose: Longer lens, exactly level with Zenny on her own warm leaf, the background collapsed to soft green haze — she is settled at her properly-filled pollen sacks with her flat stare already aimed off-frame at him, and behind her one stem is still oscillating from whatever just went past.
shots.cutInMotivation: This cut buys the scene's core change — altered power and a completely new point of view — by abandoning him at the peak of his claim; keeping him in frame with her would hand us the habitual two-shot and let his motion contaminate the stillness that makes her land.

shots.purpose: The wipe that makes it worse — the smear across his eyes is authored here, and it is his own paw that blinds him, so the crash that follows has a visible author.
shots.performanceAssignment: He scrubs with the brisk efficiency of a bee tidying himself for inspection — the paw dragging flat and hard across the band, sweeping the same route twice because a second pass is obviously thoroughness, his eyes screwed shut under the scrubbing and his head turning into each stroke to meet the paw. The drag shears the gold sideways rather than lifting it, banking it up over his eye ridges until it sits across both eyes, and when he opens them he is looking through his own mess: the head makes two quick searching turns, the hover drifting off its line as he does. He does not stop and he does not wipe again. The chest swings forward and the shoulders drag back into the launch position, the hind legs tuck, and he drives forward out of frame on a line he has not looked down — clipping a stem on the way past because he never saw it, the stem snapping back behind him.
shots.camera: Close and travelling with him again, pulled back into the wingman register by his body: as the paw finishes its drag and the chest squares, the camera is already being towed into the launch and loses his line as it goes wide across the field. It should be behind and late enough that we do not see what he is about to hit.

shots.purpose: Arrive late on the aftermath — legs kicking above a blossom rim before we ever see what put them there — then let him pop up and announce the sound effect we already heard.
shots.performanceAssignment: Wedged head-first, he treats being stuck as a job in progress: both legs pedal hard above the petal rim, the wings beating fast and shoving against the outside of the petals, and each shove rocks the whole flower on its stem. One leg finds the rim and braces; the brace lets his shoulders drive upward and force the rim wide, and the rim's spring-back dumps the bloom's own packed gold down over the mask he arrived with. He comes up out of it with the head already lifting, drags the chest forward and the shoulders back into the biggest stance in the scene so far, both antennae snapping erect on the accent, and puts the announcement out at full volume with the caked face turned proudly along the field — no dusting off, no checking himself, nothing in him treating this as a recovery.
shots.camera: The camera has genuinely missed the crash and admits it: it discovers the kicking legs past a foreground petal, the swinging branch reading behind them as the only evidence of the impact, then the pop-up pushes the frame back as his body comes up. It must not swing over to her at the end — this beat's whole engineering is that the hold she would normally get is being withheld.
shots.openingPose: Bee-height across a blossom cluster, the camera arriving into the aftermath — a branch still swinging in the mid-ground where something was swatted out of the air, and beyond it two legs kicking above a blossom rim, the rest of him buried head-first inside the bloom, gold dust still raining down through the shaft of light between us and him.
shots.cutInMotivation: The cut is the gag: skipping his blind flight and landing in the aftermath makes the audience reconstruct the impact, which the treatment holds is funnier than the impact — staying continuous through the branch and the tumble would show them everything and buy nothing.

shots.performanceAssignment: He is still working the dive when the rumble arrives, and his body takes it before his mind does: one whole side of his flight drops away so he hangs crooked, the altitude sagging low and then over-correcting too high in a single porpoise he never asked for, the caked face swinging as the tilt swings him. shots.purpose: The boast IS the launch — and the flower has the last word, closing on him. The only impact with no ride before it, and the only one he cannot cover up, because the cover-up is stuck inside a bloom.
shots.performanceAssignment: The claim and the launch are one movement in him: the chest pumps forward on the answer and the pump itself is what drives him, so he is already travelling as the words go out, antennae proud-erect, hind legs trailing, the line rising and dipping under him without ever levelling. He does not slow, does not look down the line and does not brake — the head and chest drive past the bloom's centre and compress its inner petals, and his own speed rolls the outer petals inward over his shoulders until they fold shut behind him and grip at his waist. What is left outside keeps insisting: his rear half wags side to side against the closed petals as he shoves forward at something he cannot reach, and both wings beat fast and continuous outside the fold, working against a flower that has already won. The wagging gets smaller but does not stop, and the petals do not open.
shots.camera: The camera is his wingman one final time — towed forward on his drive, close and late, and it stays with the flower after he has gone into it rather than following him inside; the petals fold across the lens's view of him and the frame simply keeps watching the closed bloom. Then it lets the far background carry the cost: the cooled sky behind the open sky stays small and sharp in the depth of the same frame, never re-established, and her leaf is never revisited — she does not turn to look and the camera does not go to ask her.
shots.openingPose: Bee-height in the field with Fuzzby driving forward into the shot from behind the lens, chest pumped on the boast, and dead ahead of him in the mid-ground an open flower waiting wide — cooling grey-green haze filling the field beyond it, gold light thinning across the petals.
shots.cutInMotivation: Her flat warning has to be allowed to finish and land before his answer arrives, and the collision of the two grammars requires the boast to begin in his moving frame, not to grow out of her still one — cutting is what makes his answer read as an interruption of the weather rather than a reply to it.

A lavender stem clips his trailing wing and the clip yaws his whole body off its line; the yaw throws his head out in front of him; that wing corrects far too late, and the late correction drives his face square into the pollen centre of a big daisy at full speed. Still travelling and half blind, his shoulder catches a second flower head and that contact turns him over — the turn becomes three fast tight somersaults, readable as three, limbs tucked, wings helpless: he is a passenger, not a performer, and every rotation happens down among the blooms at flower height, never up in open sky, with Zenny working head-down in shot the whole time. He stands up out of the finish, beats the gold off his chest with two quick swipes, and one fast embarrassed glance goes round the flowers to check whether anyone saw. envelope.prompt:
ENGLISH DIALOGUE ONLY, spoken in English. Use @Audio1 as the sole source of dialogue, wording, voice, performance and timing. The first spoken section belongs only to Fuzzby — his mouth moves only while his own words are heard, and Zenny's mouth stays closed throughout it. The second spoken section belongs only to Zenny — her mouth moves only while her own words are heard, and Fuzzby's stays closed. No other speech from anyone. Fuzzby's happy working hum, breaths and Zenny's caught, held breath are part of the performance and are directed, not banned.

Reference roles: @图1 only for the exact opening composition and positions; @图2 only for Fuzzby's identity, proportions, features and accessories; @图3 only for the world. Zenny is the smaller bee in @图1 — match her exactly as that frame shows her, every feature and accessory. Fuzzby is the character from @图2 — match the reference 100%, every feature and accessory exactly as shown; he is the bigger bee at every distance in this shot and never wears glasses.

Shot 1: one continuous take, no cuts. 50mm, starting as a close single on Zenny and widening into a two-shot as the camera travels with her — it does not chase Fuzzby into the flower and it never leaves the two of them. Begin exactly on @图1. Wide open wildflower meadow, warm low sun flaring in from upper right through banks of purple, red and white blooms that fall away into soft haze; loose gold from Fuzzby's crash is still sifting down past his stripes.

Zenny turns her face off the lens toward Fuzzby at frame left and pushes off her clover; the push tips the leaf and it dips and springs behind her as she goes, and the camera swings left with her, losing the tight single and opening out so both bees share the frame at the same distance from the lens — he stays left of her the whole way, larger in frame than she is. She arrives a body-length short of him and simply watches, hands lowered, wings ticking over; her face is already faintly working, lips pressed, a small held stillness with life in it.

Being watched winds him up. His hum climbs, his chest pumps out, his wings pick up speed and drive him off the clover to the nearest bloom, where the petal rim catches his feet and swings the whole head toward him. He drives his face straight into the pollen centre — right to the eyeline — and the bloom takes his weight, the head compressing under him and rocking back and forth on its bending stem while he burrows and works in there. Only his face enters. His striped body, his beating wings and both antennae stay outside the bloom and readable in silhouette against the bright haze; the bloom never swallows him. The rocking head shakes loose gold into the air behind his shoulders.

Then the petals let go and spring back, and the rebound pops him upright clear of them — and across his top lip and cheeks sits a thick even band of gold pollen, shaped exactly where a moustache sits, loose powder clinging to fur, never a beard, never a full-face coating, never a worn accessory. Gold puffs off the disturbed bloom behind him as he lifts. He has no idea it is there. He beams, squares his shoulders, and turns to Zenny with his chest out.

The moustache reaches Zenny's eyes first and her whole face fights her: the corners go up, she hauls them back down, her wings stutter once out of rhythm, her breath catches and holds behind clamped lips. She does not laugh and she does not speak; the fight keeps running under everything that follows.

During the first spoken section of @Audio1, Fuzzby asks her his question, sincere and bright, chest still pumped, wings fast, the gold band riding on his lip while he says it; Zenny's mouth stays shut, eyes flicking once to his lip and back to his eyes. As the second spoken section of @Audio1 begins, Zenny answers him flat and unhurried — no grin, no build, no relish, her body barely moving — while the small twitch keeps running at the corners of her mouth right through the words. Fuzzby does not react to what she says and never discovers the moustache: he stays proud, turned to her, oblivious.

Foreground and background stay quiet — soft bokeh discs of low sun through blooms behind them, one or two grains of gold drifting past. Land the frame on the pair of them a body-length apart at the same distance from the lens, he left and bigger and dusted and delighted, she right and facing him, deadpan with her corners still going. Hold on the two of them for two seconds after the audio finishes — wings still ticking, gold still drifting, her mouth still fighting. No further speech.
